title: StartLux-Decision v1.1 AutoThink: released-weights inference and mechanism reconstruction

paper.title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions

claims.statement: A readout returns a probability over each explicitly listed option; option-letter logits are temperature normalized.
AutoThink generates a thought when first-pass top probability is below the gate, with modes never/always/auto.
The final decision combines first and post-thought probabilities using a configurable mixture.
The released 27B checkpoint is described as a Qwen3.5 architecture AutoThink model.
RLCD² is reported to optimize the improvement of proper scores after deliberation, penalized by excess thought length.
Published decision benchmark scores are reference results, not independently reproduced measurements in this project.

unknowns.question: What exact examples and preprocessing produced the v1.1 released training mixtures?
Are complete RLCD² training scripts, intermediate checkpoints and optimizer state publicly available?
Can existing released weights identify which stage caused particular parameter updates?
How faithfully do offline gate simulations approximate live auto gating under stochastic sampling?
Does the selected gold dataset contain independent, sufficiently hard problems requiring deliberation?

license_note: The official inference source is Apache-2.0; the released StartLux weights are CC BY-NC 4.0. Respect both licenses.
